requiredCases.evidence: DeviceGrantV1 carries deviceId, display identity metadata/fingerprint (display-only, never attestation), authenticated user/session binding, approved scopes[] and projects[], issuedAt/expiresAt (180d), revokedAt, grantGeneration. SUBMIT_INPUT stays reserved and denied; VIEW_EVIDENCE requires separate explicit consent.
Pairing issues a one-time 32-byte challenge (10 min TTL); only its digest is persisted. Claim/confirm are single-use: expired, reused, denied or scope-changed challenges create no grant.
Pending pairings capped at 100; failed-claim attempts rate-limited to 5 per 60s window; failure responses do not disclose pending-record details.
Raw challenge bytes, device tokens and session values never appear in event payloads, receipts or snapshots; storage keeps digests only.
Restart test: pairing records and grant credentials persist across Store re-open.
rollbackPairing revokes every active grant and bumps grantGeneration while canonical local state is preserved.
CursorV1 binds owner, deviceGrantGeneration, filterDigest, schemaVersion(1), fixed upperSeq and afterSeq; HMAC-signed by a host-custodied key persisted as a hostSecret excluded from snapshots/events.
Cursor rejects on tampering, wrong owner, wrong grant, wrong generation, wrong filter digest, bad schema version and invalid bounds.
Unavailable cursor-key custody blocks synchronization with CURSOR_KEY_UNAVAILABLE.
Revocation during paging or before emission stops old-generation delivery.
Pages emit only public task/evidence projection deltas: no transcripts, credentials, native sessions, raw private logs or artifact bytes.
Fixed snapshot upper bounds; page limits bounded to 1000 events and 1 MiB; an individually oversized delta advances safely without a cursor loop.
Filtered foreign-owner/foreign-project sequences are skipped as excluded records, not treated as missing history.
Deleted retained history or verified gaps return RESYNC_REQUIRED.
Duplicate pages are idempotent; stale/out-of-order responses do not overwrite newer client state; advance is explicit.
Fresh snapshot during resync resets sync mechanics while retaining the displayed cache; per-device project isolation holds.
D01: challenge claim fails closed for unknown/expired/reused codes with no private pending-record disclosure.
D02: cursor validation order rejects tampered/stale/mismatched cursors before any emission.
D03: resync-required states surface RESYNCING and never present a falsely current dashboard.
D04: remote input attempts reject before durable input admission; reconnecting never executes saved drafts.
D05: SUBMIT_INPUT scope is listed for honest contract representation but stays reserved and denied at approve and at every input route.
D06: transport without exact configured TLS identity + clientAuth resolves REMOTE_TRANSPORT_DISABLED; no HTTP fallback.

Settings gains a paired-devices panel: pending identity/fingerprint, requested projects/scopes, explicit evidence consent, one-time code issuance, approve/deny, active+revoked state, last-seen, revoke action; wording states read-only and that downloaded device data cannot be remotely undisclosed.
View status reports OFFLINE/RESYNCING/SYNCED/STALE; mutation controls are never enabled for remote surfaces.
Offline drafts stay editable, local and unsent; clearCache clears host-derived task/evidence/cursor state while retaining unsent drafts.
submitDraft and every remote input/operation-approval route reject with REMOTE_INPUT_DISABLED before durable admission; the local API is never bound as a remote surface.
Read synchronization and remote input are independent capability gates; enabling readSync grants no input authority.
remote.readSyncV1 and remote.submitInputV1 registered with owner m17, both default false, outside strict UI preferences; read-sync-disabled behavior independently tested.
Flags are not user preferences; test-only injection used to exercise enabled paths.
